claims.text: Cryogenic rolling followed by tailored low-temperature annealing will simultaneously increase strength and ductility in as-cast eutectic HEAs such as AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
As-cast eutectic HEAs have lamellar or rod-like eutectic microstructures.
The eutectic microstructure combines a soft FCC phase with a hard BCC phase or intermetallic compound.
Cryogenic rolling is performed at liquid-nitrogen temperature.
A subsequent low-temperature anneal can recover ductility without significant microstructural coarsening.
An anneal around 600 °C for a short duration is an appropriate condition for the proposed treatment.
The proposed treatment reduces lamellar spacing.
The proposed treatment produces an increased and refined dislocation density.
The proposed treatment improves interfaces between the soft and hard phases.
Cryogenic rolling refines the microstructure and increases dislocation density while suppressing excessive dynamic recovery and retaining higher stored energy.
The subsequent anneal causes controlled recrystallization or recovery primarily at interphase boundaries.
The combined treatment increases work-hardening capacity and delays necking.
Relative to an untreated as-cast baseline, the treatment will increase yield strength by approximately 20–30%.
Relative to an untreated as-cast baseline, the treatment will maintain or modestly increase ductility.
The treatment will be effective only when processing avoids phase instability and microstructural coarsening.
Large compositional changes, including extreme Cr contents, may prevent the same strength–ductility outcome.
The magnitudes of the strength and ductility gains depend on alloy composition and processing parameters.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant simultaneous increase in both strength and ductility relative to the control would falsify the hypothesis.
